problem: A particle moves with a constant acceleration of $(3i+2j)\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}.$ The velocity of the particle is $(-7i-6j)\,\text{m/s}$ when $t=0\,\text{s}.$ Find the time when the velocity of the particle equals $2i\,\text{m/s}.$

feedback.problem: A particle moves with a constant acceleration of $(-i+7j)\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}.$ The velocity of the particle is $(2i-5j)\,\text{m/s}$ when $t=0\,\text{s}.$ Find the time when the velocity of the particle equals $(3i+2j)\,\text{m/s}.$
feedback.worked_solution:
Recall that when a particle moves with constant acceleration, the velocity vector at time $t$ can be found using

$$
v=u+at,
$$

where $u$ is the initial velocity, and $a$ is the acceleration of the particle.

Substituting 

$$
a=-i+7j,\,u=2i-5j,\,v=3i+2j
$$

into the equation above, we can attempt to solve for $t,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =u+at \\ 3i+2j & =(2i-5j)+(-i+7j)t \\ i+7j & =(-i+7j)t \\ i+7j & =-ti+7tj\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the $i$ and $j$ components in the last equation, we obtain

$$
{\begin{aligned}1=-t \\ 7=7t\end{aligned}
$$

which has no solution.
